subject: Creativity
title: Children's Imaginary Friends: Normal or Concerning?
description: A quick win: understand Children's Imaginary Friends: Normal or Concerning?.

hook.text: About 65% of children have imaginary friends by age 7. Parents worry. Psychologists celebrate.

buildup.text: Imaginary companions aren't signs of loneliness. Children with them tend to be MORE socially skilled, not less.

discovery.text: They serve as practice partners for social skills — children rehearse conversations, conflicts, and emotions safely.

twist.text: Children with imaginary friends score higher on theory-of-mind tests — better at reading others' minds.

climax.text: Many writers and actors had imaginary friends. The habit of inhabiting other minds often becomes art.

punchline.text: Imaginary friends aren't a phase to outgrow. They're creativity in training.

quiz.question: What do studies show about children with imaginary friends?
options: They have better social skills and theory of mind
